creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Muster already isolates two of the three things that matter and neither of the other two is obvious from reading the code, which is how both went unnoticed until a real launch exposed one.

**What is isolated today.** The daemon runs under herdr session `muster` on its own socket (`sessions/muster/herdr.sock`), and Muster never reads `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`. So it cannot accidentally attach to whatever daemon the user last started. That part works.

**What is not: the environment.** `daemon::start` inherits the launching process's environment wholesale, and `daemon.rs` says so deliberately - the socket path was computed from that environment, so building a fresh one risks binding somewhere else. Sound reasoning, unbounded consequence: *everything else* is carried too, into a process that outlives the app and hands it to every shell it ever spawns.

Observed 2026-08-15, not hypothesised. Launching Muster from inside a Claude Code session put `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` and `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN` into the daemon. Every pane opened afterwards inherited them - a Claude Code started in one silently disabled transcript saving and was handed another session's IPC credentials. The daemon outlives the app, so it persisted after that Muster was gone. For a tool whose entire purpose is running coding agents, leaking the launching session's agent environment into every agent it runs is close to the worst version of this bug.

**What is not: the configuration.** `discovery::config_base` is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/herdr`, which is the user's own herdr config directory. Muster's daemon is a separate session reading somebody else's `config.toml` - their `default_shell`, `shell_mode`, plugins, update checks. A herdr setting changed for their own use silently changes what Muster's panes do, and Muster's corpus was recorded against neither.

**And it should be hard to get wrong.** Today any shell can run `muster.app/Contents/MacOS/muster` and whatever that shell was carrying becomes permanent daemon state. The launch that produces a clean daemon and the launch that poisons one look identical and neither says anything.

Worth deciding rather than defaulting:

- **What the daemon is entitled to inherit.** `PATH`, `HOME`, `TERM`, locale and the XDG vars the socket path came from are the plausible list; an allowlist is the shape, since a denylist has to keep up with every tool that invents a variable.
- **Whether the panes inherit the same set as the daemon.** They are different questions: a person wants their shell to work in a pane, which argues for more, and nobody wants another session's tokens, which argues for less.
- **Whether Muster's daemon gets a config directory of its own**, and what happens to somebody who deliberately wants their herdr settings to apply.
- **How a launch says which it did.** A run log line naming what was scrubbed is the cheapest version and probably enough.

Related: the daemon has no lifecycle on quit either - see the daemon-lifecycle card.
title: 🧪 Muster's daemon should be its own world, not a session inside somebody else's
